newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia Musi refinery ups capacity by 10,000-bpd.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Musi refinery ups capacity by 10,000-bpd.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil firm Pertamina has raised the capacity at its Musi refinery in southern Sumatra to 145,000 barrels per day (bpd) since August, from 135,000 bpd, a refinery official said on Wednesday.
The increase was made possible by upgrading two small redistillation units to form one crude distillation unit (CDU), Swasono Adi Poertjahjo the refinery's general manager told Reuters.
He was in Singapore to speak at a downstream oil conference.
After the upgrading, Musi has six CDUs, and will be able to raise the refinery's diesel, kerosene, aviation turbine fuel, naphtha and gasoline output, he said.
The upgrade will also enable the new CDU to process a different crude, South Sumatra Light, instead of Duri crude which is the feedstock at other units, he said.
He said the upgrading works were carried out by the refinery's own engineering team at a cost of around 500 million rupiah.
Swasono told the conference that due to a surge in demand and limited supplies of oil products in Indonesia, a substantial addition in refining capacity was required.

He said Pertamina will start a mini refinery in Sorong, Irian Jaya near Papua New Guinea by April 1997, he said. The 10,000-bpd refinery will cater for demand from the eastern-most areas in Indonesia.

The biggest refinery complex at Cilacap is undergoing debottlenecking to raise its crude processing capability by 16 percent from the current 300,000 bpd. Production of lube oil will also be raised by 70 percent.
The project, which costs $633 million, is scheduled for completion by early 1999.
The 250,000-bpd Balikpapan refinery on Borneo island was also undergoing upgrading to allow it to handle sour crudes.
Swasono said Pertamina was also waiting for government approval to build new secondary processing units at several refineries.

The Musi, Cilacap and Balikpapan refineries plan to each build a 1,300-tonne-per-day (7,670 bpd) catalytic cracker. The Musi refinery was also seeking approval to build a methanol and methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) plant.

Two refineries in Sumatra are also seeking approval to raise their total processing capacities. The 45,000-to-50,000-bpd Sungai Pakning refinery, which is linked to the Dumai refinery complex in central Sumatra, would be revamped to raise its capacity to 100,000 bpd.

Pertamina was seeking approval to raise the capacity of a CDU at the 120,000-bpd Dumai refinery, Swasono said. There are also plans to improve the processing of residues into more valuable middle and light distillates at Dumai refinery, he said.

Indonesia imports between two and three million barrels of diesel and up to one million barrels of jet-kerosene fuel a month. The country's diesel demand is growing at 6.1 percent a year, kerosene demand growth at 4.2 percent and gasoline at 7.1 percent.

Indonesia's domestic refineries, which currently have combined production capacity of around 990,000 bpd, meet about 75 percent of the country's gas oil demand, placing its diesel imports at about 105,000 bpd, Swasono said.
